title: Frontend engineer
summary: Builds the part of a product people see and touch: interfaces that are fast, accessible and work on every screen.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The web platform every framework sits on.

stages.title: Core stack
stages.caption: A typed language, a component framework and how state flows through it.

stages.title: Tooling and quality
stages.caption: Build, test and ship with confidence.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: What separates senior frontend work: rendering strategy, performance and design systems.

title: Backend engineer
summary: Builds the services, APIs and data layer behind a product, and keeps them correct and reliable under load.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: One server language well, and how the web talks.

stages.title: Core stack
stages.caption: A framework, a database and the habits that keep data consistent.

stages.title: Shipping it
stages.caption: Package, test and deploy your service.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Systems that span many machines and many teams.

title: Full-stack engineer
summary: Owns a feature end to end, from the database to the button, usually in one language across both sides.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The web platform plus one language for both sides.

stages.title: Core stack
stages.caption: One framework that covers UI and server, plus a database and auth.

stages.title: Shipping it
stages.caption: Test, deploy and watch what you ship.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: The trade-offs you own when you own the whole feature.

title: Mobile developer
summary: Builds apps for phones and tablets, native or cross-platform, that feel fast and work offline.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: A mobile language and how apps live on a device.

stages.title: Native UI
stages.caption: The declarative UI toolkits on each platform.

stages.title: Cross-platform
stages.caption: One codebase for both stores.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: The services and polish real apps need.

title: DevOps / platform engineer
summary: Builds the paths code takes to production and keeps the systems it runs on healthy, repeatable and observable.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The operating system, networks and a scripting language.

stages.title: Containers and delivery
stages.caption: Package everything the same way and ship it automatically.

stages.title: Infrastructure
stages.caption: Clusters and clouds, described as code.

stages.title: Reliability
stages.caption: Know when things break, and break less.

title: Data engineer
summary: Moves, cleans and models data so analysts and models can trust it, in batch and in real time.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: SQL, a data language and how databases store things.

stages.title: Pipelines
stages.caption: Extract, transform, load, on a schedule.

stages.title: Warehouses and lakes
stages.caption: Where analytics data lives at scale.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Streaming and the modern lakehouse.

title: Machine learning engineer
summary: Trains, evaluates and serves models, and turns research results into reliable product features.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The maths and the Python stack underneath every model.

stages.title: Classical ML
stages.caption: Learning from labelled data, and knowing when it's working.

stages.title: Deep learning
stages.caption: Neural networks and the frameworks that train them.

stages.title: Production
stages.caption: From notebook to a model people depend on.

title: AI application engineer
summary: Builds products on top of large language models: retrieval, agents, evaluation and guardrails.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: How LLMs work, at the level an app builder needs.

stages.title: Retrieval
stages.caption: Give the model the right context.

stages.title: Agents and tools
stages.caption: Let the model act, safely.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Measure quality and keep it safe.

title: Security engineer
summary: Finds and fixes weaknesses before attackers do, and builds systems that stay safe when something fails.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Networks, operating systems and the basics of cryptography.

stages.title: Identity and access
stages.caption: Who are you, and what may you do?

stages.title: Application security
stages.caption: The bugs that show up again and again.

stages.title: Offense and response
stages.caption: Think like an attacker, respond like a defender.

title: Game developer
summary: Builds interactive worlds: gameplay code, rendering, physics and the tools artists use.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: A performance-minded language and the maths of space.

stages.title: Engines
stages.caption: Where most games are built today.

stages.title: Graphics
stages.caption: How a frame gets drawn.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Worlds that generate themselves, and new platforms.

title: Embedded engineer
summary: Writes the software inside devices, close to the hardware, where memory and timing are tight.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: C, memory and how a computer actually runs code.

stages.title: Microcontrollers
stages.caption: Talking to hardware directly.

stages.title: Real-time systems
stages.caption: Deadlines that must never be missed.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Connected devices and Linux on the edge.

title: Data scientist
summary: Turns data into decisions: asks the right question, tests it with statistics and builds models when they help.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The maths and the language most analysis is done in.

stages.title: Analysis
stages.caption: Clean the data, explore it and test what you see.

stages.title: Modelling
stages.caption: Classical models first, and an honest way to evaluate them.

stages.title: Communicating and going further
stages.caption: Results only matter once people understand them.

title: Data analyst
summary: Answers business questions with data: queries, spreadsheets and dashboards that people actually use.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Spreadsheets, SQL and the statistics behind a fair comparison.

stages.title: Analysis
stages.caption: Pull the right data and look at it from every side.

stages.title: Dashboards
stages.caption: Put the answers in front of the people who need them.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Model the data once, and tell the story behind it.

title: Site reliability engineer
summary: Keeps production fast and up: sets reliability targets, builds the monitoring and leads the response when things break.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The systems everything runs on.

stages.title: Running services
stages.caption: Containers, orchestration and the infrastructure as code that builds them.

stages.title: Observability
stages.caption: See what the system is doing before users tell you.

stages.title: Reliability practice
stages.caption: Targets, budgets and learning from failure.

title: Cloud architect
summary: Designs how a company's systems run in the cloud: secure, resilient and not more expensive than they need to be.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: What the cloud is and the networks it is made of.

stages.title: Core services
stages.caption: Compute, storage and data on the big clouds.

stages.title: Architecture
stages.caption: Patterns for systems that scale and survive failures.

stages.title: Governance
stages.caption: Security, code-defined infrastructure and the bill.

title: MLOps engineer
summary: Takes models from a notebook to production and keeps them working: pipelines, serving, monitoring and retraining.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Enough ML and software engineering to talk to both sides.

stages.title: Training pipelines
stages.caption: Reproducible data, experiments and features.

stages.title: Serving
stages.caption: Put models behind an API that scales.

stages.title: Keeping models healthy
stages.caption: Watch what models do once real data arrives.

title: QA and test automation engineer
summary: Makes sure software works before users find out it doesn't: test strategy, automation and quality gates in CI.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: What to test, at which level, and why.

stages.title: Automating tests
stages.caption: Frameworks for every layer of the app.

stages.title: Beyond functional tests
stages.caption: Speed, security and the edge cases people miss.

stages.title: Quality in delivery
stages.caption: Tests that run on every change and stay trustworthy.

title: Blockchain developer
summary: Builds smart contracts and the apps around them, where bugs are public and money is on the line.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The cryptography and data structures a blockchain is built from.

stages.title: Blockchains
stages.caption: How chains agree and what they can run.

stages.title: Building contracts
stages.caption: Write, test and deploy contracts on the EVM.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Scaling, proofs and keeping contracts safe.

title: Mainframe developer
summary: Maintains and modernizes the COBOL systems that still move most of the world's money.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: What a mainframe is and why it is still here.

stages.title: Core skills
stages.caption: The language, the batch jobs and the online transactions.

stages.title: Data
stages.caption: The databases mainframe programs read and write.

stages.title: Modernization
stages.caption: Bringing old systems into the present without stopping them.

title: Enterprise applications developer
summary: Customizes and connects the platforms companies run on: CRM, ERP, workflow and integration.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: What business systems do and the data behind them.

stages.title: Platforms
stages.caption: The big suites and their own languages.

stages.title: Integration and automation
stages.caption: Make the systems talk and remove manual steps.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Low-code tools and the architecture that ties it together.

title: Audio software engineer
summary: Writes the code behind plugins, music apps and game sound, where a late sample is an audible glitch.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: How sound becomes numbers and back.

stages.title: Signal processing
stages.caption: Filters, synthesis and compression.

stages.title: Tools and frameworks
stages.caption: The DAWs and frameworks audio products are built with.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Real-time constraints, games and space.

title: Automotive and aerospace software engineer
summary: Writes software for cars, aircraft and spacecraft, where it has to be proven safe before it runs.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Embedded C on real-time hardware.

stages.title: Vehicles
stages.caption: How the software in a car is organized.

stages.title: Safety
stages.caption: Standards and the evidence they demand.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Flight software, models and autonomy.

title: GIS and mapping developer
summary: Builds maps and location features: storing places, analysing them and drawing them fast on any screen.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Coordinates, projections and the shape of geographic data.

stages.title: Data and analysis
stages.caption: Store and analyse places at scale.

stages.title: Web maps
stages.caption: Draw maps in the browser.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Routing, indexing and imagery.

title: E-commerce and CMS developer
summary: Builds the stores and content sites businesses run on, from themes to headless storefronts and payments.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The web basics every store is built on.

stages.title: Content management
stages.caption: Publishing tools, classic and headless.

stages.title: Commerce
stages.caption: Catalogues, carts and the platforms that run them.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Fast, findable storefronts.

title: Compiler and language engineer
summary: Builds the compilers, runtimes and tools that turn code into fast, correct programs.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The theory of languages and the machine underneath.

stages.title: Front end
stages.caption: From text to a checked syntax tree.

stages.title: Back end
stages.caption: From the tree to optimized machine code.

stages.title: Runtimes
stages.caption: Running code fast once it's compiled.

title: Penetration tester
summary: Breaks into systems with permission, then explains how to stop the real attackers doing the same.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Networks, operating systems and the web, from an attacker's view.

stages.title: Reconnaissance
stages.caption: Learn the target before touching it.

stages.title: Exploitation
stages.caption: Turn a weakness into access.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Deeper exploits, red teams and responsible reporting.

title: Robotics engineer
summary: Makes machines sense, decide and move: from motor control to perception and planning.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The maths and code a robot runs on.

stages.title: Moving
stages.caption: Kinematics, dynamics and control loops.

stages.title: Sensing and planning
stages.caption: Know where you are and where to go.

stages.title: Software and going further
stages.caption: The robotics software stack and learning-based control.

title: Quantum software engineer
summary: Writes programs for quantum computers and figures out which problems they can actually help with.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The linear algebra and physics behind a qubit.

stages.title: Circuits
stages.caption: Gates, circuits and the toolkits that build them.

stages.title: Algorithms
stages.caption: Where quantum computers could beat classical ones.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Noise, error correction and the hardware.

title: Product designer
summary: Designs how a product works and feels, grounded in research with the people who use it.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: How people perceive, think and act.

stages.title: Research
stages.caption: Find out what people need before designing.

stages.title: Design
stages.caption: From flows to a polished, consistent interface.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Measure the result and design responsibly.

title: Bioinformatician
summary: Uses code and statistics to read genomes, compare sequences and model the molecules of life.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Programming, statistics and the algorithms biology leans on.

stages.title: Sequences
stages.caption: Read DNA and compare it.

stages.title: Analysis
stages.caption: Turn reads into biology.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Structure, simulation and medicine.

title: Quantitative developer
summary: Builds the pricing models and trading systems where mathematics meets microseconds.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: The maths of chance and the languages of finance.

stages.title: Modelling
stages.caption: Price instruments and measure risk.

stages.title: Trading systems
stages.caption: Fast, correct systems that trade.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Data and the payment rails underneath.

title: Hardware design engineer
summary: Designs digital chips, from logic gates to a verified design ready for silicon or an FPGA.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.caption: Logic, numbers and how transistors switch.

stages.title: Describing hardware
stages.caption: Write hardware as code.

stages.title: Verification and synthesis
stages.caption: Prove it works, then turn it into gates.

stages.title: Going further
stages.caption: Processors, open silicon and chips for AI.
